chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Wasshash, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no harm with the fish that the Magian catches.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by Zoroastrians permissible to eat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this hadith from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the fiqh of *kitabiyyun* (People of the Book) in the Iranian context, where Zoroastrians were often classified as such. The ruling establishes that their fishing methods are valid for consumption, distinguishing this from other acts of worship or slaughter which may have stricter conditions. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of accepting the general practice of *Ahl al-Kitab* in matters of food procurement unless explicitly prohibited.
